rubric: keep unchanged if a session makes $500+; keep and tweak if the average is $200+; rework if below that or the account breaches

expected_pace.note: the $55 is arithmetic at a 78% win rate minus $4.98 costs; the $95 is the retracted report's own figure and is kept only to show why the 3-day target cannot be planned

survival.model: one signal per session, all contracts share the outcome, 40% consistency, stop-first, $4.98 round trip; 4000 walks, horizon 286 sessions at 0.21 trades/session
survival.note: size lowers survival on this rule: $700 per stop is 70% of the buffer. The old 82% pass for two micros came from drawing an independent outcome per contract and is retracted (RESEARCH-LOG (t)).

provenance: Book from RESEARCH-LOG (n). Entry ordering corrected per (o) item 1: the instruction is a BUY LIMIT at the prior-day low, not a buy stop below the market. Win rate, pass rate and replay in (n) are retracted as evidence until edge_causal.py has run.

evidence.inconsistency: median 14 sessions cannot follow from $95/trade at 0.21 trades/session: that needs 13 trades, about 62 sessions. One of the two figures was computed at a different size or on a different book. (s) records this.

size_rule: One micro, and do not escalate on win-rate grounds. At a 78% win rate two micros lowers the pass chance from 76% to 65% because one stop is $700 of a $1,000 buffer. Two micros only becomes the better size above an 85% win rate (83% pass), which nothing here has measured.
why_this_one: Of every family in the 287,280-config sweep it is the only one whose order type can actually be placed, its risk is 35% of the buffer instead of 70-100%, and the 0.5R target needs 67.6% wins rather than 84%.
